description:
What is awkward: crate-jmap-chat-types/src/push.rs:366-382 (chat_message_push_preserves_vendor_extras) asserts that a vendor field 'acmeCorpBatchId' round-trips, but does NOT assert that the '@type' wire tag does NOT end up in the .extra map. The combination of #[serde(tag = "@type", rename = "ChatMessagePush")] on a struct AND #[serde(flatten)] for extra is exactly the kind of serde corner where the test commit message's claim 'works correctly with the #[serde(tag)] tag rename' is plausible but not proven.

If a future serde release (or refactor) regressed the tag-vs-flatten interaction such that '@type': 'ChatMessagePush' leaked into extra, the test would still pass — both the typed accountId/state/messages fields and the vendor acmeCorpBatchId field deserialize fine, and on re-serialize the extra would dump '@type' alongside the tag-emitted '@type', producing duplicate keys or a corrupted payload. Neither failure shows up under the current assertions.

Suggested rewrite: add explicit negative assertions to this test (and to the parallel EphemeralMessage Enable/Disable/Typing/Presence preserves_vendor_extras tests in ephemeral.rs):

    assert!(!push.extra.contains_key("@type"),
        "the discriminant tag must not leak into extras");

Same pattern applies to ChatStreamEnable / ChatStreamDisable / ChatTypingEvent / ChatPresenceEvent extras tests — they all assert positive vendor-field round-trip but none negatively assert that the enum's @type discriminant didn't bleed through serde flatten.

Cost is one extra assertion per affected test (5-6 sites). Benefit is a real serde-regression tripwire for one of the explicitly-novel combinations introduced by 2957e6e.
title: ChatMessagePush '@type' extras-preservation test does not verify @type is excluded from extra
